newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 96-97 soybean imports seen at 2.6 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 96-97 soybean imports seen at 2.6 mln T.

text.p: Mexico will import around 2.6 million tonnes of soybeans in the 1996-97 cycle, the chairman of the Guadalajara-based Chamber of Western Oilseed Manufacturers said Monday.
"Mexico will have its lowest ever soybean harvest (in the cycle which runs from October 1 to September 30)," Gonzalo Cardenas Jimenez told Reuters.

Cardenas said the drought was one of the reasons for the expected historical output levels, forcing imports -- for use in the edible oil and fats industry -- to increase just less than 400,000 tonnes over the 2.23 million tonnes expected to be imported by the end of the 1995-1996 cycle.

The leader, whose members produce 66 percent of the total output of oils and fats in the country, said around 95 percent of soybean imports come from the United States and the rest from other nations, usually headed by Brazil.
Cardenas said Mexican soybean production is expected to drop to 50,000 tonnes this calendar year, down from the 135,000 tonnes in 1995.
